chunk.title: Customer Communication Standard
chunk.content: Use plain language that customers can understand and an accessible text format on the status page. For a physical-site interruption, coordinate signage and contact-centre guidance so customers receive consistent information. Tell staff the safe service alternative before opening it to customers. Where impact scope is uncertain, identify the affected service without inventing a count. Route individual customer claims to Customer Service for review; this standard establishes communication content and timing, not compensation amounts or a universal payment promise.

SEV1 first notice is due within 15 minutes and updates every 30 minutes; SEV2 first notice within 30 minutes and updates every 60 minutes under POL-COM-001. Avoid publishing unverified repair forecasts or identifying affected individuals. If capacity is uncertain, state the uncertainty before encouraging travel to another centre. Restoration messages distinguish site reopening from completion of investigation and outstanding follow-up.

A restoration notice does not replace a missing earlier update. Record any missed deadline and its reason in the timeline for review.

chunk.title: Business Continuity Procedure
chunk.content: Activate the continuity assessment immediately for an unsafe site or a multi-site essential-service closure. For a customer-facing digital or payment outage lasting 60 minutes or more, the Duty Manager must decide whether to activate the approved continuity plan and record the decision and rationale. The 60-minute threshold is an assessment deadline, not permission to delay SEV1 escalation at 30 minutes. POL-INC-001 and POL-INC-002 continue to apply during continuity. Safety takes priority over maintaining transaction throughput.

chunk.title: Incident Classification Standard
chunk.content: HarbourLink Services classifies disruptions affecting customer centres, online services, payments, facilities and operational records. An incident is an unplanned service interruption or integrity failure that needs coordinated response. The recorder captures discovery time, affected service and site, observed impact, current owner and unknown facts. A service request without disruption is not an incident. The incident record must label estimated values as estimates; an unknown impact must not be recorded as zero. One incident may affect multiple functions but has one coordinating owner.

chunk.title: Incident Classification Standard
chunk.content: Severity 1 (SEV1) applies when at least 500 customers are affected, when a customer-facing digital or payment service is continuously unavailable for 30 minutes or longer, or when there is credible immediate danger to people. A multi-site closure that prevents essential customer service is also SEV1. Any one threshold is sufficient. An outage lasting 35 or 45 minutes therefore meets the duration threshold even if the impact count is unknown. Suspected impact is validated urgently; classification is precautionary while safety facts are uncertain. Escalation is defined in POL-INC-002 section 2.
